title: A child is coming
hookLine: families pray Ardas and read Gurbani while waiting for a birth
tomorrow: the baby's here. what's the first thing the family says?

lines: A CRIB STILL IN ITS BOX.
cards: A crib still in its box. A bag packed by the door. A group chat that lights up at every twinge.

Waiting for a birth has its own weather. So what do you pray for a child who isn't here yet? Sikh families waiting turn to Ardas and to Gurbani, and some sing a blessing Guru Arjan wrote in a mother's voice.

teach.b: It's on ang 496, and it opens: son, this is your mother's blessing. In paraphrase: may you never forget the Lord, not for an instant. May the True Guru be kind to you, and may you love the company of the holy.
May the Lord's protection be your clothing, and singing his praise your food.
Drink the nectar, live long, and in remembrance find joy without end. Look at what's on the list, and what isn't. No riches, no fame, no grades.
And Ardas is how a family brings its hope before the Guru: standing together, remembering the Gurus, and then adding their own request for the mother and the child.

teach.h: HANNAH: FOR THIS CHILD I PRAYED.
teach.b: A shared thing across a border: in the Hebrew Bible, shared by Jews and Christians, Hannah weeps and prays at the sanctuary for a child, and later says, "For this child I prayed; and the LORD hath given me my petition which I asked of him."

A hoped-for child carried to God in prayer: Sikh families would know that. And an honest difference. Hannah prays alone, in silence, her lips moving, with a vow to give her son to the LORD all his days.
Ardas is prayed standing together, by the family or the sangat, out loud.

how: While a family waits for a birth, Sikhs pray Ardas for the mother and child, at home or in the gurdwara, and read or listen to Gurbani; some sing Guru Arjan's mother's blessing (ang 496).

games.q: what does “a child is coming” mean?
o: a fast the mother keeps until the baby arrives
a vow to give the baby to the gurdwara's service
waiting for a birth, held in Ardas and Gurbani

games.q: waiting for a child — tap the pairs.
p: a mother's blessing for her son
prayed in silence for a child

s: Guru Arjan's mother's blessing asks wealth and success for the child
it asks that the child never forget the Lord; its food is praise, its clothing the Lord's protection.
Hannah prayed in silence, her lips moving
and later said: for this child I prayed.
Sikh families pray Ardas while waiting for a birth
standing together, they add their request for the mother and child.

games.q: Maya's grandma tells the story of Hannah praying for a child. Maya asks if Sikhs have anything like it. what's a fair answer?
o: yes: families carry a hoped-for child to God in Ardas; Hannah prayed alone, with a vow.
yes, exactly the same: Sikhs make Hannah's vow and give the child to the gurdwara.
not really: Sikhs don't pray before a birth, only give thanks once it's over.
games.why: shared: a hoped-for child brought to God in prayer. different: Hannah prays alone, silently, with a vow; Ardas is prayed together, out loud.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind someone waiting for a child, or a family with a new arrival on the way. Hold their names for the length of the sit. If you pray, ask for them; if not, simply wish them well.

wordCard.voice: A child is coming. The waiting, held in Ardas and Gurbani: a mother's blessing that asks for remembrance.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: asees, a blessing: the word at the start of the mother's blessing on ang 496.

carryVoice: Your line: waiting with prayer. The waiting isn't empty when it's held like this. Stay close to your phone.
